items.stem:
Identify the soil with the help of following information.
(1) It develops in areas with high temperature.
(2) It is the result of intense leaching due to heavy rain.
(3) Humus content is low.
Options
items.answer: High temperature together with heavy rain causes intense leaching, which washes the lime and silica out of the soil and leaves a soil poor in humus. These are exactly the conditions under which laterite soil develops. Hence the soil described is laterite soil.

items.stem: Which of the following statement defines Sustainable Development ?

options.label: A
options.text: Sustainable use of natural resources without considering the need of the future generation.

options.label: B
options.text: Present generation fulfils its needs while considering the needs of the future generation as well.

options.label: C
options.text: It means utilisation of natural resources by the past, present and forthcoming future generation.

options.label: D
options.text: To meet the needs of the future generation even if the needs of the present generation go unmet.

items.answer: Sustainable development means development that takes place without damaging the environment, so that the present generation meets its own needs while the ability of future generations to meet theirs is not compromised. That is option (b).

items.stem: In which of the following states is black soil found?
items.answer: Black (regur) soil is formed from the Deccan lava and covers the plateau of Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and parts of Gujarat. Of the four states listed, black soil is found in Gujarat.
items.ocr: Option (c) is printed 'Raiasthan'; read as Rajasthan.

items.stem:
Assertion - Alluvial soil is ideal for growth of paddy, wheat, cereal and pulse crops.
Reason : Alluvial soil is well-known for is capacity to hold moisture.
items.assertion: Alluvial soil is ideal for growth of paddy, wheat, cereal and pulse crops.
items.reason: Alluvial soil is well-known for is capacity to hold moisture.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Alluvial soil is rich in potash, phosphoric acid and lime, which is why paddy, wheat, cereals and pulses grow so well on it, so the assertion is true. Its high moisture-retaining capacity is the quality of black soil, not of alluvial soil, so the reason is false.
items.ocr: The printed reason reads 'well-known for is capacity'; kept as printed.

items.stem: Which among the following is a type of resources classified on the basis of exhaustibility?
items.answer: On the basis of exhaustibility resources are divided into renewable resources, which can be renewed or reproduced, and non-renewable resources, which take millions of years to form. Hence the answer is renewable and non-renewable.

items.stem: Which one of the following options best signifies this cartoon?

options.label: A
options.text: Shows the reality of current Indian Bureaucracy System.

options.label: B
options.text: The co-ordination among such organization is generally rare.

options.label: C
options.text: People's management is essential for energy project.

options.label: D
options.text: Derail of development projects that were meant for community.

items.answer: The cartoon shows a community cart being pushed one way while contractors, bureaucrats and the government project board pull the other way, leaving everyone confused. It makes the point that a project succeeds only when the people themselves manage it. Hence option (c).
items.ocr: The printed solution reads 'People's management is essential for every project' while option (c) prints 'for energy project'; the option letter (c) is unambiguous, so the wording difference is a book typo, not a key conflict.

items.stem:
Assertion - Resources are free gifts of nature.
Reason : Resources like soil, air, water are easily available in nature.
items.assertion: Resources are free gifts of nature.
items.reason: Resources like soil, air, water are easily available in nature.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Resources are not free gifts of nature; they are the outcome of the interaction of nature, technology and institutions, so the assertion is false. Materials in the environment become resources only when human beings have the technology and the institutions to use them, so calling them easily available gifts is false as well.

items.stem: Select the intensively leached soil of the monsoon climate.
items.answer: Laterite soil develops in areas of high temperature and heavy rainfall, where the heavy monsoon rain leaches the soil intensively and leaves it low in humus. So the intensively leached soil of the monsoon climate is laterite.

items.stem: What is plantation of trees on a large scale to check soil erosion termed as?
items.answer: Planting trees on a large scale over land that was not forested is called afforestation, and it is one of the standard methods of checking soil erosion.

items.answer: Individual resources are those privately owned, such as one's own plots, houses and plantations. Burial grounds and public parks are accessible to all members of a community, so they are community owned resources. Hence A is own plots, houses and own plantation and B is community owned resources.

items.stem: What is the name of the report Brundtland Commission published?
items.answer: The Brundtland Commission brought out its report in 1987 under the title Our Common Future, the report that introduced the widely used definition of sustainable development.

items.stem: Which of the following is a root cause for resource depletion at the global level according to Mahatma Gandhi?

options.label: C
options.text: Greedy and selfish individuals and exploitative nature of modern technology

items.answer: Gandhiji held that there is enough for everybody's need but not for any body's greed. He placed greedy and selfish individuals, together with the exploitative character of modern technology, at the root of resource depletion at the global level.

items.stem:
Assertion - The availability of resources is not the only necessary condition for the development of any region.
Reason : Not only availability of resources but also corresponding change in technology and institutions is necessary for development of any region.
items.assertion: The availability of resources is not the only necessary condition for the development of any region.
items.reason: Not only availability of resources but also corresponding change in technology and institutions is necessary for development of any region.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Regions rich in resources can still remain backward, so availability alone does not bring development; the assertion is true. Development follows only when resources are matched by corresponding changes in technology and institutions, which is precisely why availability is not enough. The reason is true and explains the assertion.

items.stem: Which is the right sequence of the soil profile?

options.label: A
options.text: Topsoil , Substratum weathered parent rock material,subsoil, Unweathered parent bed rock

options.label: B
options.text: Substratum weathered parent rock material, Unweathered parent bed rock,subsoil , topsoil

options.label: C
options.text: Topsoil, Unweathered parent bed rock, Substratum weathered parent rock material,subsoil

options.label: D
options.text: Topsoil, subsoil, Substratum weathered parent rock material, Unweathered parent bed rock

items.answer: A soil profile read downward from the surface runs topsoil, then subsoil, then the substratum of weathered parent rock material, and finally the unweathered parent bed rock. That is the order given in option (d).

items.stem:
Match the following and choose correct option.
Column-IColumn-II
A.Terrace farming1.Different crops grown parallely
B.Strip cropping2.Hill slopes are used as cultivable land in the form of flat cut regions of slope
C.Contour ploughing3.Along the slope of mountain
D.Crop rotation4.Different crops grown in systematic succession
Option :
items.answer: Terrace farming cuts flat steps into a hill slope, so A goes with 2. Strip cropping grows different crops in parallel strips, so B goes with 1. Contour ploughing is done along the slope of the mountain, so C goes with 3. Crop rotation grows different crops in systematic succession, so D goes with 4. The match is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.
items.ocr: The book prints options (b) and (c) with identical text 'A - 4, B - 1, C - 3, D - 2'; reproduced as printed. The key (a) is unaffected.

items.stem: What is not true about Agenda 21?

options.label: A
options.text: It aims for achieving Global Sustainable Development.

options.label: B
options.text: It is an agenda to fight environmental damage, poverty, disease etc.

options.label: C
options.text: Agenda 21, has legal powers to acquire even private property for public good.

options.label: D
options.text: One of its major objectives is that every local govt. should draw its own agenda 21.

items.answer: Agenda 21 is a declaration signed at the Rio Earth Summit of 1992; it aims at global sustainable development, at fighting environmental damage, poverty and disease through global cooperation, and it asks every local government to draw up its own local Agenda 21. It carries no legal power to acquire private property, so statement (c) is the untrue one.

items.stem:
Assertion - Land is a natural resource of utmost importance.
Reason : Land can be used for various purposes.
items.assertion: Land is a natural resource of utmost importance.
items.reason: Land can be used for various purposes.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Land is of utmost importance because we live on it, carry out our economic activities on it and draw our support systems from it, so the assertion is true. It is precisely because land supports so many different uses - farming, forestry, mining, settlements, industry, roads - that it is so important. The reason is true and explains the assertion.
items.ocr: Stem and legend option (a) are on page 4; options (b)-(d) and the answer continue on page 5.

items.stem: Which type of the erosion can be seen in the given picture?
items.answer: The picture shows running water cutting deep channels into clayey soil and carving the land into a badland of ravines. Erosion of this kind, where water makes deep gullies in the soil, is gully erosion.

items.stem: Which of the following is a root cause for resource depletion at the global level according to Mahatma Gandhi?

options.label: C
options.text: Greedy and selfish individuals and exploitative nature of modern technology

items.answer: Gandhiji blamed greedy and selfish individuals, and the exploitative nature of modern technology, for the depletion of resources at the global level, summing it up as enough for everybody's need but not for any body's greed.
items.ocr: The book repeats question 13 verbatim here with a different board tag.

items.stem: Who was against mass production and wanted to replace it with the production by the masses ?
items.answer: Gandhiji opposed mass production and argued for production by the masses, that is production carried on by many people using simple means rather than by machines in a few hands.

items.stem:
Match the following items given in column-I with those in column-II. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below :
Column-IColumn-II
A.Contour ploughing1.Planting lines of trees.
B.Strip cropping2.Western and Eastern Himalaya.
C.Shelter belts3.Grass are left to grow between crops.
D.Terrace cultivation4.Decelerate the flow of water
Option :
items.answer: Ploughing along the contour lines slows the flow of water down a slope, so A goes with 4. In strip cropping strips of grass are left to grow between the crops, so B goes with 3. Shelter belts are lines of trees planted to break the wind, so C goes with 1. Terrace cultivation is practised in the Western and Eastern Himalaya, so D goes with 2. The match is A-4, B-3, C-1, D-2.

items.assertion: Resource planning is an easy process in India.
items.reason: Resource planning involves planning structure, identification and inventory of resource across the regions.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

items.answer: Resource planning in India is a complex, not an easy, process, because resources are distributed very unevenly across the country, so the assertion is false. The printed key also treats the statement about the planning structure and the inventory of resources as false, giving both assertion and reason false.

items.stem: Which of the following is a root cause for resource depletion at the global level according to Mahatma Gandhi?

options.label: C
options.text: Greedy and selfish individuals and exploitative nature of modern technology

items.answer: For Gandhiji the root of global resource depletion lay in greedy and selfish individuals and in the exploitative nature of modern technology, not in the mere use of resources.
items.ocr: Third printing of the same question in this section (see 13 and 20); stem begins on page 5 and the options finish on page 6.

items.stem:
Identify the land-
• Includes rocky, arid and desert areas.
• This land put to other non-agricultural uses includes settlements, roads, railways industry etc.
• Continuous use of this land over a long period of time without taking appropriate measures to conserve and manage it, has resulted in land degradation.
Select the appropriate option from the following.
items.answer: Rocky, arid and desert tracts, along with land put to non-agricultural uses such as settlements, roads, railways and industry, are grouped in the land-use records as waste land and land put to other non-agricultural uses. The land described is therefore waste land.

items.stem: At the international level Club of Rome advocated resource conservation for the first time in ___.
items.answer: The Club of Rome was the first body to advocate resource conservation at the international level, and it did so in 1968.

items.answer: Black soil holds moisture well and is the classic cotton soil, so A is cotton. The soil that is very fertile and rich in potash, phosphoric acid and lime, on which sugarcane, paddy and wheat are grown, is alluvial soil, so B is alluvial soil.

items.stem: Who presented Gandhian philosophy in his book Small is Beautiful?
items.answer: Schumacher restated Gandhiji's philosophy of resource use in his 1974 book Small is Beautiful.

items.stem:
Identify the personality-
• He was very active in voicing his concern about resource conservation.
• His words were: “There is enough for everybody’s need and not for any body’s greed”.
• He placed the greedy and selfish individuals and exploitative nature of modern technology as the root cause for resource depletion at the global level.
• He was against mass production and wanted to replace it with the production by the masses.
Select the appropriate option from the following.
items.answer: The quotation about enough for everybody's need but not for any body's greed, the charge against greedy individuals and exploitative technology, and the call for production by the masses are all Gandhiji's. The personality is Gandhiji.

items.stem: When was the Brundtland Commission formed and its report published?
items.answer: The Brundtland Commission published its report Our Common Future in 1987, which is also the year given as the answer.

items.stem:
Assertion - Soil is the most important renewable natural resource.
Reason : Soil supports different types of living organisms on earth.
items.assertion: Soil is the most important renewable natural resource.
items.reason: Soil supports different types of living organisms on earth.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Soil is indeed the most important renewable natural resource, since it renews itself over time and everything we grow depends on it, so the assertion is true. It is the medium of plant growth and supports many kinds of living organisms, and that is exactly why it is the most important renewable resource. The reason is true and explains the assertion.

items.stem: What is the name of the report Brundtland Commission published?
items.answer: The Brundtland Commission's 1987 report was titled Our Common Future.

items.stem: The most widespread relief feature of India is
items.answer: About 43 per cent of India's land area is plain, which is more than the share of either the mountains or the plateaus. The plains are therefore the most widespread relief feature of India.

items.stem: Which relief feature provides facilities for tourism and ecological aspects?
items.answer: Mountains feed the perennial rivers, carry the forests and the snow cover, and draw visitors to hill stations, so they are the relief feature that serves both tourism and the ecological system.

items.stem: Identify the land which is 27% under a certain relief feature.
items.answer: Of India's total land area, about 43 per cent is plain, 30 per cent mountain and 27 per cent plateau. The relief feature covering 27 per cent is therefore the plateau.

items.stem: The deep cracks in the soil during hot weather formed due to-

options.label: C
options.text: Due to presence of excessive fine clay.

items.answer: The picture shows black soil, which is made of very fine clay particles and has a strong affinity for water. In the hot dry weather the clay loses that moisture and contracts, so the surface splits into deep wide cracks. All three reasons given are therefore correct.
items.ocr: Stem, picture and options (a)-(b) are on page 7; options (c)-(d) and the answer continue on page 8.

items.stem: What is the gross cropped area ?

options.label: A
options.text: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year plus net sown area

options.label: B
options.text: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year minus net sown area

options.label: C
options.text: Area sown with crops but is counted only once.

options.label: D
options.text: Double of the area sown more than once in an agricultural year

items.answer: The gross cropped area counts every sowing in the year, so it is the net sown area plus the area that was sown more than once in that agricultural year.

items.stem:
Assertion - Arid soil is unsuitable for cultivation.
Reason : Arid soil is generally sandy in texture and saline in nature. It restricts the filtration of water.
items.assertion: Arid soil is unsuitable for cultivation.
items.reason: Arid soil is generally sandy in texture and saline in nature. It restricts the filtration of water.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Arid soil, being sandy, saline and low in humus and moisture, is generally unsuitable for cultivation unless it is irrigated, so the assertion is true. Its sandy texture in fact lets water percolate very freely rather than restricting filtration, and the calcareous kankar layer below is what checks percolation, so the reason as stated is false.

items.stem: What is the net sown area ?

options.label: A
options.text: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year plus net sown area

options.label: B
options.text: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year minus net sown area

options.label: C
options.text: Area sown with crops but is counted only once.

options.label: D
options.text: Double of the area sown more than once in an agricultural year

items.answer: The net sown area is the land actually put under crops in an agricultural year, each piece counted once no matter how many times it was sown. That is option (c).
items.ocr: The printed solution line is garbled and truncated - '(c) Net area sown more than once in an agricultural' - but the key letter (c) matches the printed option 'Area sown with crops but is counted only once', which is the correct definition of net sown area, so (c) is kept.

items.stem: What is the percentage of the culturable waste land in India?
items.answer: In the reported land-use figures for India, culturable waste land accounts for 4.41 per cent of the total reporting area.

items.stem: Fallow land is a kind of agricultural land. It is ________ fertile.
items.answer: Fallow land is arable land left uncultivated for one or more agricultural years so that it can recover its fertility. Because it is resting, it is less fertile at that moment than the land under crops, so the blank is filled with 'less'.

items.stem:
Match the following columns :
Column-I (Type of Soil)Column-II (Crops Grown)
A.Arid soil1.Cotton and groundnut
B.Black soil2.Jowar and Bajra
C.Laterite soil3.Tea and coffee
D.Mountain/ Forest soil4.Cashew and spices
Option :
items.answer: Arid soil of the dry western region carries the hardy millets jowar and bajra, so A goes with 2. Black soil is the cotton and groundnut soil, so B goes with 1. Laterite soil of the Western Ghats grows cashew and spices, so C goes with 4. Mountain and forest soil of the hill slopes grows tea and coffee, so D goes with 3. The match is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

items.stem:
Arrange the following types of soil found as the major soil types in India from north to south-
1. Forest and mountainous soil.
2. Black soil.
3. Alluvial soil.
4. Red and Yellow soil.
Option :
items.answer: Moving from north to south, the Himalayan belt carries forest and mountainous soil, the northern plains below it carry alluvial soil, the Deccan lava region carries black soil, and further south and east lies the red and yellow soil. The order is 1, 3, 2, 4.
